channel.title: Battery Sensei
channel.description: Updates for Battery Sensei — a quiet macOS menu-bar battery utility.

item.title: Version 1.0.0
item.description:
1.0

Battery Sensei is the menu-bar battery utility I wanted but couldn't find. One that knows my calendar.

It reads your next four hours of meetings and warns you before your battery dies during one. At -30, -15, -5, or -1 minutes. You pick. Event titles never leave your Mac.

It also does the usual: charge cap with weekly recalibration, per-app battery use over the last hour / day / week, and a soft history strip so you can see what your battery has been through.

Five languages. macOS 14 or later. Apple Silicon or Intel.

Drag it into Applications.

item.title: Version 1.1.0
item.description:
1.1

Sharper meeting alerts and a real Settings window.

You now pick exactly which checkpoints fire before each meeting: -30, -15, -5, -1. Default is -30 and -5. The toggle chips match the website. Changes apply the moment you flip them.

The Settings window stops vanishing when you click another app. (It used to. Sorry.)

Other small things:

  • "Latest forecast" stays put when no meeting needs warning about. Empty state reads "No conflicts" instead of disappearing.
  • Hover states on snooze buttons and reminder chips, finally.
  • "Show event titles" replaces "Hide event titles". Default is on.
  • Live "N min left" countdown actually counts down now.

item.title: Version 1.1.1
item.description:
1.1.1

Sparkle now downloads and installs updates silently. You won't see another "Install update?" prompt unless you opt out in the dialog.

Two layout fixes: the Activate Pro button matches the Buy button's height again, and the Latest forecast card aligns to one column instead of three.

item.title: Version 1.2.0
item.description:
1.2

One-click activation after you buy.

Click "Open Sensei & activate" on the thank-you page and the app opens with your license key already typed in. You click Activate. That's it. No more copy-paste from the email.

Also: the in-app Buy button now drops you straight into the checkout flow instead of bouncing through the marketing page.

item.title: Version 1.2.1
item.description:
1.2.1

Two reliability fixes.

The "Install and Relaunch" window now actually comes to the front when Sparkle has an update ready. Previously the app was a menu-bar accessory and the prompt could be born behind whatever you were doing.

Activating a new license no longer risks leaving you locked out. The new key gets activated first; the old one only releases if the new one succeeds. Network blip, typo, cancelled mid-flow — your existing license stays put. The sheet now shows a small warning when you're about to swap.

item.title: Version 1.2.2
item.description:
1.2.2

Settings polish.

The settings window no longer floats above other apps' full-screen Spaces. Standard window ordering applies: click the full-screen app behind it and the settings drops behind, like every other Mac window.

The menu-bar display picker (Percent / Time / Icon) got a once-over. All three battery glyphs are now the same width regardless of which mode you pick. The selected tile is outlined in red in light mode and white in dark mode — border only, no background fill, so the preview strip behind reads through.

Manage and Run Setup Wizard Again lost their trailing dots, along with Settings, Share image, Activate Pro, Check for Updates, and Check now. Cleaner action labels across the app.

License section: Manage Subscription is now a proper accent link with hover, matching how Manage Activations already looks in the activation sheet. Remove from this Mac stays a bordered button — destructive actions earn deliberate buttons.

Activating a different license key no longer risks locking you out. The new key is activated first; the old one only releases if that succeeds. Failed network, typo, sheet cancellation — your existing license stays put. The activation sheet shows a small warning banner when you're about to swap so you know what's happening.

item.title: Version 1.2.3
item.description:
1.2.3

Quieter idle, sharper feedback.

Battery Sensei now does noticeably less work when nothing's happening. The menu-bar charging pulse runs at half the previous rate (still reads as motion, half the redraws), the icon render cache holds 4× more entries so the percent/time display stops thrashing, and the meeting forecast only re-publishes when the predicted severity actually changes. A few CPU hot spots in the per-app history store got cleaned up too.

Hover affordances filled in across the app. Every interactive surface, including the warning-mode wizard cards, the language picker, the saga search clear button, and the rescue-receipt dismiss, now responds to pointer-over with a subtle scale lift and pointing-hand cursor. Six gaps closed.

Removing a license from this Mac now asks first. Confirmation dialog explains the slot returns to your pool, and the destructive button is clearly labeled. Hover on the button is consistent with the Manage link beside it.

The settings window stops floating above other apps' full-screen Spaces. Click a full-screen app behind it and the settings drops behind, like every other Mac window.

A few visual fit-and-finish bits: the Lifetime badge corner radius now matches the Remove button beside it, the hero card kanji watermark lights red on hover like all the other cards, and the menu-bar icon picker has a uniform battery glyph width across Percent / Time / Icon.
